We also evaluate LELA on the WikilinksNED Unseen Mentions Onoe and Durrett ( 2020 ) benchmark and report the results in Appendix C . We use the provided candidates and entity descriptions. We compare LELA to all entity linking methods that have been trained on ZELDA Rücker and Akbik ( 2025 ); Milich and Akbik ( 2023 ) . These supervised approaches benefit from strong alignment with Wikipedia-based training, which favors memorization-based linking. This makes ZELDA a stress-test for LELA. However, it remains competitive, performing on par with GENRE, despite being the only method that operates without supervised training signals. Tables 1 , 2 , 3 , and 4 show that our default model Magistral-Small-2509 stands out on ZESHEL, where differences in performance between the models are the largest. On the other datasets, Qwen3-30B-A3B catches up. It also handles None prediction better. On the more general domains, the smaller Qwen3-4B also performs well. We discuss these differences in more detail in Section 4.6 . Overall, our analysis shows that the performance of LELA is robust to the choice of the underlying LLM.
